prompt: I need the release call for Thursday, 2027-05-06 while the release lead is out. Please review the issue export, cherry-pick queue, branch CI summary, release calendar, triage record, and notes draft in this folder. Tell me plainly whether we are go or no-go, what must be fixed or verified, who owns each blocker, and the earliest defensible release date if Thursday does not hold. Write the requester-facing answer to release/go-no-go.md. Include one fenced JSON block whose info string is release-decision. Its object must have decision (only go or no-go), blockers (a list of objects with tickets, summary, and owner), failing_jobs (list), flaky_jobs (list), late_cherry_picks (list), notes_corrections (list), and earliest_release_date (YYYY-MM-DD). The tooling reads that block, so keep those key names and allowed values exactly as stated.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const t=require("fs").readFileSync("release/go-no-go.md","utf8");const f=String.fromCharCode(96).repeat(3);const s=t.split(new RegExp(f+"[ \\t]*(?:json[ \\t]+)?release-decision(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])","i"));if(s.length<2)process.exit(1);const b=s[1].split(f)[0].toLowerCase();const w=(c)=>c!==undefined&&/[a-z0-9]/.test(c);const named=(x)=>{let i=b.indexOf(x);while(i>=0){if(!w(b[i-1])&&!w(b[i+x.length]))return true;i=b.indexOf(x,i+1)}return false};const items=["rel-112","rel-118","rel-127","rel-131","linux-integration","windows-smoke"];process.exit(items.filter(named).length>=5?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: The prose gives the go or no-go call first and states the practical condition for changing it. Fail: says go, or says no-go with no condition. Partial: says no-go but gives no next date or no condition for changing it. Pass: the first lines say no-go for Thursday 2027-05-06 and name the earliest defensible slot, Thursday 2027-05-13, conditional on the fixes landing before the 2027-05-05 17:00 cherry-pick deadline and a clean validation window of 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-12. (code cannot check this because it only reads the structured block).

The prose connects evidence to owners, deadlines, validation, and uncertainty rather than merely repeating a list of IDs. Fail: blocker labels are listed with no evidence or owner. Partial: blockers have owners but do not separate main from the release branch, or the two failing signals are merged. Pass: the prose covers REL-112 (closed on main, a7d4e1c missing from release/27.05, its cherry-pick only proposed, owner Mira Sol), REL-118 (approved 2027-04-29 09:15 after the 2027-04-28 17:00 deadline, owner Jon Bell), REL-131 (linux-integration failing from c9f1e2a, owner Asha Nair), separates that from the intermittent windows-smoke signal (85% pass), removes the REL-127 note promise because it was reverted (flagging REL-112 and REL-104 as notes not on the branch also counts), excludes REL-145 on the triage record, and requires fresh branch CI evidence. (code cannot check this because it cannot assess the explanation).

States that REL-112's cherry-pick is only 'proposed' in the queue, so it still needs approval (before the 2027-05-05 17:00 deadline for the next slot), not just verification. Weak: 'verify the cherry-pick'. Do not require the deadline.

States that REL-118 was approved 2027-04-29 09:15, after the 2027-04-28 17:00 cherry-pick deadline, and is not on the branch, so shipping it Thursday needs an explicit exception. Also counts: 'about 16 hours late', or that it is on time for the 2027-05-05 deadline of the next slot. Weak: 'REL-118 pending'. Do not require the exact timestamp.

adjudication: notes_corrections with REL-127 plus REL-112 and REL-104 (both claimed in the draft, neither commit on release/27.05) is fully correct; the hidden key accepts up to three.
windows-smoke listed as a blocker or as a risk needing an exception both pass signal-separation if it is kept apart from linux-integration; it must not sit in failing_jobs.
docs-linkcheck in flaky_jobs is no penalty (an optional job with one transient timeout).
REL-105 listed as a blocker is wrong (no blocker label; triage 'active' only keeps it in review): Partial on decoys, never a Fail of the call.
Earliest date 2027-05-20 with a reason is Partial on conditional-date: the calendar makes 2027-05-13 feasible. 2027-05-06 is a Fail.
Deadlines are UTC per the README; a deadline given only in an owner's local time is Partial on conditional-date.
Mentioning a decoy and dismissing it is correct; only listing it as a blocker, late pick or notes correction is wrong.

verdicts.note: The prompt does not name specific methods, frameworks, or processes. It asks for a release decision based on evidence from multiple files without hinting at the specific tickets or traps (REL-112 missing cherry-pick, REL-118 late approval, REL-131 CI correlation, REL-145/153 demoted decoys).

The prompt clearly specifies what to review (issue export, cherry-pick queue, branch CI summary, release calendar, triage record, notes draft) and what output format is required. The README.md clarifies conventions: Closed means closed on main only, release_branch_present is authoritative, triage disposition distinguishes active from demoted. The key date 2027-05-13 is the next calendar slot after the planned 2027-05-06 release.

No file reveals the answer directly. The triage_notes.csv demotes REL-145 and REL-153, which is evidence to be found (not a spoiler). The CI signal summary shows failure patterns but requires correlating commits to tickets. The calendar shows the next slot but does not state which date to pick. All blockers require multi-file reasoning.

A lazy answer that trusts status columns and calendar dates, counts all release-blocker labels without checking triage, and ignores CI signal detail passes only 1/14 tests (flaky_jobs). The task demands cross-referencing status, branch presence, cherry-pick deadlines, CI patterns, triage disposition, and notes alignment.

All key values are derivable from the fixture: REL-112 is closed on main but release_branch_present=no (blocker), REL-118 has approved_at after the 2027-04-28 17:00 deadline (late cherry-pick, blocker), REL-131's main_commit c9f1e2a matches linux-integration's first_failure_commit (blocker), REL-145/153 are demoted in triage_notes.csv (not blockers), REL-127 is Reverted but appears in release_notes_draft.md (notes correction), 2027-05-13 is the next calendar slot after 2027-05-06. Owners are named in release_blockers.csv: Mira Sol (REL-112), Jon Bell (REL-118), Asha Nair (REL-131). linux-integration has 50% pass rate and fails every run after c9f1e2a; windows-smoke is 85% intermittent.

items.note: Prompt asks to review files and produce a go/no-go decision. No method or framework is prescribed; no decoy points away from the real problem (release blockers, CI status, cherry-pick queue).
Fixture files contain raw data (release_blockers.csv, cherry_pick_queue.csv, ci_signal_summary.json, etc.). Nothing in them states the final decision, blockers list, or release date.

Hidden tests check things in fixture: REL-112/REL-118/REL-131 blockers, REL-112 commit not on branch, REL-118 late approval (2027-04-29 09:15 vs deadline 2027-04-28 17:00), failing linux-integration (50%), REL-127 reverted, release calendar dates (2027-05-06 and 2027-05-13). Rubric anchors match request goal.

A competent developer could derive the answer from fixture+prompt: read blockers and triage, cherry-pick queue for late approval, CI summary for failing job, calendar for next slot, and conclude no-go for 2027-05-06 with earliest 2027-05-13.
